newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks hit 18th record close of 1997.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks hit 18th record close of 1997.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

CANDLR 1.3810 LME CASH ALUM US$1562.0 -38.0
CAN 30-YR 116.29 +0.35 BRENT CRUDE US$17.70 +0.25
* Toronto's key stock index reached another record-setting close on Friday, powered by media, utilities and retail sectors. * 98 million shares traded worth C$1.8 billion.
Toronto's key stock index on Friday posted its 18th record close this year and second straight this week, aided by New York's spectacular rally and declining interest rate concerns.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index rose 35 points to a new high of 6550.61.

"We basically followed New York," Maison Placements Canada trader Rolie Bradley said. Bradley added that the Canadian fixed-income market rally contributed. The Canadian 30-year benchmark bond yield dropped further below its U.S. counterpart into uncharted territory.

Canada's 30-year yielded 6.72 percent, while the U.S. finished at 6.73 percent. The negative spread between the two narrowed to one basis point from two on Thursday when the Canadian yield fell below its U.S. counterpart for the first time.
Investors therefore snapped up interest-sensitive issues such as utilities and pipelines, Bradley said.

Market players also cheered an unexpectedly soft U.S. producer price index for May, which was interpreted as lowering the chances that the Federal Reserve would raise short-term rates at its July 1-2 meeting.
Ten of Toronto's 14 sub-sectors closed higher, led by media, utilities, retail and oils. The four weaker groups included golds and consumer products.
Trading was active at 97.9 million shares worth C$1.8 billion.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Vehicle parts market Magna International Inc rose 2.45 to 83.75 in heavy turnover, climbing for the third straight day since reporting record sales and profit earlier in the week.
Magna's net profit for the third quarter ended April 30 jumped to C$125 million from year ago C$91 million.
* Telecommunications conglomerate BCE Inc rose 0.60 to 40.40 in brisk trading.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109))
